mechanism_narrative: A strong increase in GDP growth rate indicates a robust economy, leading to higher consumer spending and subsequently driving up the S&P 500 index over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during early-cycle expansions (t-test p > 0.05), or GDP growth rate does not lead to increased consumer spending.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 1.5%, it signals a tightening monetary cycle, leading to decreased borrowing and spending, and subsequently driving down the S&P 500 index over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during monetary tightening cycles (t-test p > 0.05), or federal funds rate does not lead to decreased borrowing and spending.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate indicates a weakening labor market, leading to decreased consumer spending and subsequently driving down the S&P 500 index over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during late-cycle contractions (t-test p > 0.05), or unemployment rate does not lead to decreased consumer spending.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates an increase in economic activity, leading to higher demand for goods and services, and subsequently driving up the S&P 500 index over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when industrial production increases (t-test p > 0.05), or industrial production does not lead to increased economic activity.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts increase and GDP growth rate is high, it signals a strong economy with high consumer spending, leading to increased demand for goods and services, and subsequently driving up the S&P 500 index over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when housing starts and GDP growth rate are high (t-test p > 0.05), or housing starts and GDP growth rate do not lead to increased consumer spending.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is low and inflation is high, it signals an expansionary monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing and spending, and subsequently driving up the S&P 500 index over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when federal funds rate is low and inflation is high (t-test p > 0.05), or federal funds rate and inflation do not lead to increased borrowing and spending.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate is low and payroll employment is high, it signals a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending, and subsequently driving up the S&P 500 index over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when unemployment rate is low and payroll employment is high (t-test p > 0.05), or unemployment rate and payroll employment do not lead to increased consumer spending.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production and housing starts increase, it signals an increase in economic activity, leading to higher demand for goods and services, and subsequently driving up the S&P 500 index over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO rises > 1% in 2 months and HOUST rises > 5% in 2 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when industrial production and housing starts increase (t-test p > 0.05), or industrial production and housing starts do not lead to increased economic activity.
